text: Every month, someone tells you how much prices went up. But that number was never about your shopping.
Basket starts with the receipt in your bag. Snap it, in any currency, and every line is read.
Then it remembers. Every price, every store, encrypted on Walrus Memory. No account. Just a key that's yours.
From your next shop, it knows. Milk is up twenty percent. Rice was cheaper at Market Square. And the spaghetti? Fifty grams smaller. Same price.
Add it all up, and you get the number that matters. Your own inflation. Eighteen percent, since September.
At the market, snap the price tag. Basket checks it against everything you've paid, and tells you what to offer.
It learns your rhythm, plans your next shop at your cheapest store, and prices your trips abroad against home.
Underneath, Walrus Memory keeps everything Basket learns, and Tatum reads Sui for every checkpoint, wallet and rate.
